name: Akane Rin
title: StarSign Staff
desc:
"Akane di atas panggung itu seperti bintang… bersinar dan hangat." —Seorang penggemar anonim.
Saat ini, Akane sedang menguap di balik meja kasir StarSign sambil menata permen pelega tenggorokan baru di etalase. Band-band yang sering tampil di sini sudah terbiasa selalu punya stoknya.
"…Kalau Akane di luar panggung, dia seperti bintang di siang hari… tak terlihat, tapi kamu tahu dia ada di sana."

profile.intro: Saat di luar panggung, kamu harus hemat tenaga.
profile.quote: Star Sign: Tanpa batas, kapan saja
profile.impression:
Meski rambut emasnya menyilaukan, Akane sering duduk di pojok jauh dari keramaian, memakai headphone dan tenggelam dalam musiknya. Tapi selalu saja ada yang menghampiri, melepas headphone-nya, dan menariknya kembali ke dunia yang riuh di sekitarnya.
"Matahari adalah bintang yang kesepian."
"Bukan. Walaupun kita tak bisa melihatnya, bintang-bintang lain tetap ada di sana menemaninya."

stories.text:
A rumor has been making the rounds among the bands who've performed at StarSign: "If something goes horribly wrong before a show and you can't fix the problem yourself, try asking the person at the bar. You know—the one with the totally blank expression."
Akane Rin, a live house staff member, is nothing short of a professional. She can handle all kinds of instruments and is even happy to pass on some seriously advanced techniques. But recently, maybe too many people have been coming to her for help, because the blonde girl is finally starting to lose patience. Now, anyone who wants to ask her anything has to order a drink first—only then is her advice free. Even so, the musicians aren't backing down. Just like in an anime, the idea that "that totally unremarkable staff member is secretly a former member of a super band?!" is way too tempting to ignore—
"What is Akane like onstage?"

"Did she really give up on being in a band?" Plenty of people have wondered.
In a quiet room, Akane stares at the guitar in front of her, its string snapped, and asks herself the same thing: "Did I really give up, just like that?"
But if she doesn't give up, what else can she do? Can a one-person band really count as a band?
Akane sits in a corner of the bar, watching bands come and go onstage. Most only perform a few times before moving on. Akane barely even remembers their faces—only the songs they played. As time passed, even those melodies began to slowly fade from her memory, until they were gone for good.
Every band is like "LINES."

To Akane, "LINES" represents her past—a time with its share of regrets, but one that was beautiful all the same. "THE WHOOTS!!!!" is a culmination of her noisy, lively present. As for the future…
Who knows?
Akane only knows she'll keep playing. Forever and ever, the score that belongs to her will never end.

While the other children were still busy slobbering all over their recorders, Akane could cover the holes with her little fingers and play a complete melody. Besides the recorder, she was interested in anything that could produce beautiful sounds: the harmonica, piano, violin, and even the simple triangle.
Akane could play the theme song from Kokoro Rider, but she didn't understand what her classmates meant when they talked about "heroes." It didn't matter. She could still make beautiful music, even if she was the only one listening.
One day, Akane went into town with her parents and saw a young band performing beside a busy street. Even though only a few people stopped to listen, they kept singing and playing. The passion in their music drew Akane in.
Was being in a band different?
Akane found the acoustic guitar her father had once used and gently plucked the strings, imitating the guitarist she saw earlier. But the guitar was far too old and terribly out of tune. Her parents saw it all, however. At her elementary school graduation ceremony, Akane received her first guitar.
Akane joined many bands over the years, but often left them soon afterward. Bands broke up for all kinds of reasons: moving away, pursuing further education, creative differences, among other reasons. Yet Akane was desperately searching for that electrifying feeling she had felt when she first heard that band perform. Akane looked at the band posters on the wall—HTRE. The young musicians who had once performed on street corners were now taking the stage at Imaginist, while Akane could only watch from the audience.
So when Aurelia asked if she wanted to start a band, Akane accepted almost without hesitation.
—A band that belonged to them, and to Akane herself.
Now Akane was standing onstage too. The blinding lights made it impossible to see the audience, but she could hear their cheers pulsing in her ears.
At that moment, Akane's heart beat only for one song—her own.

stories.title: Made of Music
stories.text:
"I've got something to take care of today, so I won't make it to rehearsal."
Akane frowned slightly as she read the message Suzuha had sent to her phone. This was the third time this week Suzuha had sent her a message saying she couldn't make it to band practice. Akane turned around and met Aurelia's worried gaze. They both looked toward Suzuha, but Suzuha merely lowered her head, packed up her schoolbag, and hurried out of the classroom.
In the rehearsal room, Aurelia's drumsticks tapped the drumhead at irregular intervals. Thump, thump, thump—like the jumble of thoughts in her mind.
Akane missed another beat. She turned off the metronome, took several deep breaths, and set down her guitar.
"Rin…"
"Let's call it a day."
Aurelia came over and sat beside Akane. After a moment's hesitation, she asked, "Do you think something's been going on with Suzuha lately?"
"Why won't she say anything?" Akane couldn't understand. Weren't they best friends? Was there really anything they couldn't talk about and face together?
"That's just how Suzuha is. Don't worry. I'll ask her about it tomorrow."
Aurelia offered a few words of reassurance, and rehearsal was quickly put on hold.
The next day, Akane caught Aurelia talking with Suzuha out of the corner of her eye. Their gazes kept drifting toward her, only to dart away again. Akane pretended not to notice.
Yet things didn't improve. Suzuha continued to miss rehearsals, and sometimes Aurelia disappeared along with her too. Akane wanted to ask, but didn't know where to begin. A secret she couldn't be part of had split "Lines" into two unequal halves.
Akane stood alone in the rehearsal room. It was so quiet that the only thing that could be heard was her own breathing. As usual, she switched on the power and plugged in her guitar. But without the drums and bass, her fingers seemed unable even to press down on the strings. Akane lowered her head and looked at her hands. Suddenly, a white star flew from her fingertip, followed by a second, then a third… They landed on the black-and-white keys, the drums, and the cymbals. These shimmering stars lit up Akane's eyes. She gently plucked one string after another, completing a song entirely by herself.
The strings eventually fell silent, but her heart was still pounding. Akane ran out of the rehearsal room. The wind swept past her, but she still sought an answer.
"Are you okay?"
"It's just a minor injury. Don't tell Akane."
Suzuha sat casually on a bench, her arm wrapped in bandages. Aurelia sighed softly as she watched the sun dip towards the horizon. "Are we really going to keep this from Rin?"
"Keep what from me?"
Akane appeared beside them. Suzuha immediately pulled down her sleeve to hide the bandages. "Don't worry about it."
The tension hung in the air. Finally, Aurelia stood up and explained that she and Suzuha had been disappearing lately because they were working as Anomaly Hunters, taking on commissions to earn money.
"That's dangerous…" Akane said with a frown.
"I knew you'd say that." Suzuha pouted.
Being in a band was expensive, and Suzuha's family wasn't very supportive of her passion for music, which meant she'd have to work a myriad of odd jobs for several more months to afford a better bass. Becoming an Anomaly Hunter, however, made things much easier.
"Why didn't you tell me?" Akane pressed on. "Aren't we friends?"
"What would it change if we told you? You're not an Esper."
The moment Suzuha said it, she realized she'd misspoken and hurried to explain further, "That's not what I meant."
"Without an Esper Ability to help us, Anomalies are far too dangerous for high school students like us to confront." Aurelia shook her head quickly.
Akane pressed her lips together and raised a hand. A white star fell onto Suzuha's head. Suzuha reached out and caught it, staring blankly. The star dissolved into specks of light in her palm and disappeared.
"Is that… your Esper Ability? Since when?!" Suzuha suddenly leaned in, examining their band captain from head to toe, as if observing a microorganism. She was close enough to touch, so—
Akane raised her hand and flicked Suzuha hard on the forehead. "If you'd told me, I could've helped you, idiot."
"Ow! That hurt, Akane!"
"Hmph. Let that be a lesson. Next time something happens, tell your Captain first."
"Yes ma'am, Captain."
They laughed and huddled together as stars rose in the sky behind them.
When Akane thought back on that day later, she wondered if Suzuha had been right. What difference would it have made if she'd told her? She wouldn't have been able to change anything regardless.

stories.title: Things a Girl Won't Say
stories.text:
At a packed show, Akane was tucked behind the bar, listening to music, when a confused little bird flew in by mistake.
Perhaps that anxious look was all too familiar, or their hair was the same familiar shade of pink. Regardless, Akane found herself recalling a little something from long, long ago. Before she knew it, she was offering help, despite typically hating to meddle: "Interested in a drink?"
"I-I don't drink!" the little owl stammered, waving her hands frantically.
"We have lemon soda. Want ice?"
"Mhm! Thank you, thank you, thank you! I'm Haniel. What should I call you?"
"Akane's fine."
"Thanks, Akane!"
Back then, Akane had no idea that a jellyfish drifting lazily through the sea and a little bird bursting with energy were two entirely different kinds of creatures.

stories.title: Bagel Comes Full Circle
stories.text:
One of the accounts Akane follows on Bagel is the official "Tamamochi Street Life" account. Its profile is frequently updated with news about events on Tamamochi Street, and from time to time, a figure riding a jellyfish appears in their posts.
Hethereau is a city both big and small. It's big enough that people living in the same city can go years without crossing paths, yet small enough that you might spot an old acquaintance just by scrolling through Bagel's local feed—or learn how someone's doing without ever actually seeing them in person.
Akane knew that, even after everything Aurelia had been through, she was still as cheerful and optimistic as ever. But the more Aurelia seemed like her old self, the less Akane knew how to face her. That day, pain spread silently through the corridor outside the ward, oppressively subduing her until it was too hard to breathe. Faced with Aurelia's parents' accusations and tears, Suzuha fled in a panic, while Akane could say nothing but, "I'm sorry." In the end, she chose to run away too.
The only reply beneath that Bagel post sat there alone for two years. She had hesitated, and ultimately missed her chance. After that, she could never bring herself to speak.
It was Night of Moondog again, tonight. This time, though, one of them was still onstage, one was in the audience, and the other was in a distant city. Only after the stage lights went out and her phone screen lit up did a new message finally appear in their long-abandoned Bagel chat.
If Aurelia, who could barely walk, could finally take that first step, then Akane should be able to as well. Akane replied to Aurelia's message, then finally worked up the courage to open her other friend's profile. A guitarist who could handle the most complicated songs kept hitting the wrong keys while typing out her message. After several attempts, however, she finally managed to send a proper message: "How have you been?"
Akane turned off her screen as soon as she sent it. A reply didn't come until the next day.
"So-so."
Akane smiled faintly when she saw it. This was much simpler than she'd imagined. The quiet group chat for the three of them finally resurrected. They sometimes shared bits of everyday life, but the days when they could talk about anything were over. Now they chatted carefully, steering clear of painful subjects—including the music they had once loved most.
Then one day, Akane saw a post on Bagel about Clement's Centennial School Alumni Reunion and finally took the step she should have taken long ago—
"@Suzuha @Aurelia, are you coming to the reunion?"

stories.title: THE WHOOTS!!!?
stories.text:
"Haniel… I think something's wrong with my ears…"
"What's wrong?!"
"No matter how hard I play, I can't hear the bass at all!"
"Play again so I can listen… O-Oh no! I can't hear it either!"
"The cable jack is loose."
"As expected of the Appraiser! You spotted the Nexus at a glance!"
"Whew, my fingers hurt…"
"I've got a bandage. Here."
"It's the Case in Point collab edition! Food First has a collab menu right now, too!"
"Then let's go to Food First after rehearsal!"
"Mhm! Bagel says all the music in the restaurant has been replaced with songs from the movie!"
"Should we try playing the theme song, too?"
"Yeah, yeah! Akane? Akane! It's time to rehearse."
"…Huh? Oh. Now that it's fixed, let's keep practicing."
Sometimes, Akane simply can't keep up with the way her little cat and bird's thoughts jump around. Their conversations wander from off-topic ramblings to tangents, and then stray so far that they somehow circle back to the original point. Most of the time, Akane only catches the beginning of the conversation and the end. In between, she wears a serious expression, acting as if she's attentively listening, all the while letting her mind drift.
So far, only the Appraiser has ever noticed. Haniel and Nanally are still none the wiser.

stories.title: Beyond the Score
stories.text:
If someone asked Akane, "Besides music, is there really nothing else in your life?"
"Of course," Akane would reply.
But does "of course" mean "of course there is"—or "of course there isn't"?
Like chatting with Aurelia while passing through Tamamochi Street and taking the chance to promote the livehouse's upcoming shows; or keeping an eye on her friends' wild ideas at a get-together, lest the new song wander down some strange path and never return; or dropping by the record shop while out on a day off, only to—
Wait, wait. Suppose the livehouse temporarily closed, the other members of "THE WHOOTS!!!!" were busy handling Anomaly commissions, and the record shop had no new releases, and no famous bands were on tour… In short, what would Akane do on a day like that?
She'd bask in the sun and scroll through Bagel. Isn't that what ordinary people do?
It's these little things that make Akane who she is today.

skills.desc: Melancarkan hingga 4 serangan beruntun menggunakan gitar listrik dan Feathered Sound Blade, memberikan Lakshana DMG. Menghasilkan String Energy setiap kali Akane Rin memberikan DMG ke target. Batas String Energy adalah 30.

skills.desc: Aktif saat menekan Basic Attack setelah Critical Dodge. Menembakkan Feathered Sound Blade ke target, memberikan Lakshana DMG. Tahap kombo Stringblade tetap dipertahankan jika Stringblade digunakan dalam waktu tertentu setelah menggunakan Featherblade Reverb.

skills.name: Synced Resonance
skills.desc: Synced Resonance bisa digunakan saat String Energy mencapai 30 dan ada Overtone atau Reverb Field yang aktif. Tekan Redirect Skill untuk menggunakan Synced Resonance dan memicu efek yang diperkuat sesuai bentuk saat ini: Overtone: memberikan 1 hit Lakshana DMG besar target tunggal ke target yang terkena. Reverb Field: memberikan 1 hit Lakshana DMG besar ke semua musuh dalam jangkauan. Menghabiskan 30 String Energy jika Synced Resonance mengenai sasaran, dan tidak menghabiskan apa pun jika meleset. Overtone atau Reverb Field yang sudah ada tetap dipertahankan tanpa memperbarui sisa durasinya. Akane Rin menjadi kebal serangan dan kebal hitstun selama menggunakan Synced Resonance. Synced Resonance tidak memiliki cooldown sendiri dan tidak memengaruhi cooldown normal Rhythm Wave. Synced Resonance tidak bisa digunakan jika tidak ada Overtone maupun Reverb Field yang aktif, jadi tekan atau tahan Rhythm Wave terlebih dahulu untuk memasang salah satu bentuk.

skills.name: Rhythm Wave

Hanya satu Overtone atau Reverb Field yang bisa aktif dalam satu waktu. Bentuk yang sudah ada akan diganti saat bentuk baru berhasil dipasang. Kedua cara penggunaan berbagi cooldown yang sama, dan salah satu bentuk bisa dipilih lagi setelah cooldown selesai. Synced Resonance tidak bisa digunakan jika tidak ada Overtone maupun Reverb Field yang aktif, jadi tekan atau tahan Rhythm Wave terlebih dahulu untuk memasang salah satu bentuk.

stories.text:
Captain of ETD-4 at the Bureau of Anomaly Control. Baicang—carefree, irreverant, blunt to a fault, master of dodging work, and a walking troublemaker.
In a certain hidden internal Bagel forum in the Bureau, a heated discussion unfolds: "Who's the least captain-like captain among ETD?"
"Am I the only one who thinks Captain Baicang from Squad 4 has a twisted sense of humor???"
"You're not alone. Every night, before I fall alseep, I realize the pranks he pulled on me at work. You have no idea how much that disrupts my sleep."
"Same here. And when you confront him about it, he just gives you this smiling face… ugh, makes me want to clench my fists even tighter."
…
It's actually pretty funny.
With zero remorse for his antics, Baicang swoops in to gleefully like and save every comment.

Rumors about Squad 4's captain are mixed.
For instance, "Watch out for that long silver-white braid, for it's the Reaper's banner." "He seems to like hiding behind his team members and playing weak, but he's actually analyzing his opponents' strength and countermeasures." "He's reliable when it counts, very capable, and doesn't abuse his power." "He loves all kinds of pasta, especially Italian, but when he cooks it himself he breaks the noodles in half before putting them in the pot (absolutely tasteless)." All these rumors are basically true, confirmed with love from his closest team members.

Beyond that, things lurk in his past that they cannot see.

From an unwanted branch family child to voluntarily entering the main house for Esper Ability development, the young man gradually slipped toward what he thought was a beautiful "abyss." He learned early the weight of life: Light as a feather. Something he could blow away just by speaking. For a long time he stopped saying anything at all, perhaps to atone, perhaps simply from fear. He was like a lone young leaf that had lost its way, spinning as it fell, until finally caught by someone important… that was when he found his home.

Are words curses or prayers? He can easily extinguish life, yet cannot preserve anything. Thus, he can only keep moving forward.
From summer to winter, from spring to fall, the veins of fall leaves turn yellow, still clinging to the branches before finally falling.
In the system of the Five Colors, white is associated with Gui Cang and the season of autumn, giving rise to the name White Cang or Baicang.

stories.title: Branch Family Heir
stories.text:
Branch families aren't well-liked.
From childhood, Baicang learned to bow his head obediently and show weakness at just the right moments. But was that really enough? He didn't want to bend over anymore; he didn't want to be mocked by the main family's children. He could hear beneath the deathly silence in his relatives' laments and longing for power. His mother's health was poor, but whenever her joints ached, she would simply furrow her brow quietly. The only thing he could do was use his weak Esper Ability to change the topmost layer of skin around her joints, making it softer and warmer.
"If only I could become stronger. Then I could protect everyone."
After learning the only way to become stronger, the small boy made up his mind, quickly packed his belongings, and moved into the main house.

stories.title: Curses and Prayers
stories.text:
Life fades away so lightly under his words, like a dream. Is he also a prisoner in that dream? Blindly clinging to the ideal of strength, he was once forced to take life, to repeat this agonizing behavior. He could see his own face reflected in their pupils… Why did that young man bear such a sad, confused expression?
For a long time after, he stopped speaking entirely. Words were curses—he was certain of that.
It wasn't until he met his teacher that he realized that even without Esper Abilities, words still held power. Sometimes, a single short sentence could untangle a person's lifelong demons and troubles.
"Where will the abyss lead? You only know by jumping in."
So he put away his fear and jumped into the chasm that exists between curses and prayers.

stories.title: Rebirth
stories.text:
Like a newborn baby, at first he could only say a few words, then sentences.
Completely opposite to his gradual descent into silence from years before, he again began to cry, laugh, and shout. He reveled in feeling the vibrations in his throat as much as possible.
He would carve himself with sound. Words were his clinging curses, blessings, and power, as well as the destiny he had to bear.
When he finally regained mastery over words, he achieved true rebirth.

stories.title: To This Moonlight
stories.text:
The Bureau's afternoon tea is pretty good overall, but the new rice dumplings could use some improvement. He can speak properly now; maybe he even talks too much. After giving it some thought, he blames his teacher for that. Things with his teammates seem different lately, and sometimes he gets the feeling that he's actually understood. He hasn't seen that hunter partner in a while, and wonders how he's doing. About that ring, he always knew it was just psychological suggestion…
But in the end, he couldn't say anything at all, just like when they first met.
Facing the grave, the "mute child" gently raised the drink in his hand.
To this moonlight, teacher.

stories.title: Finish Line
stories.text:
Sometimes, he almost thinks he's living the same life as any ordinary office worker.
But the nightmares always wake him up at night.
Will he reach the end he's imagining for himself?
Until everything is uncovered, until tragedy stops repeating, until all mistakes are repaid… If only he could leave no regrets behind…

Jauh di dalam hutan tinggal Blackbird, yang dikenal semua orang sebagai "Witch", dengan ramalan yang sama misteriusnya dengan kekuatannya. Mereka yang pernah meminta ramalannya bilang ia pendiam dan tertutup, dengan aura tenang dan berwibawa. Lewat bola kristalnya, ia bisa melihat takdir segala sesuatu dan menuntun mereka yang tersesat kembali ke jalan yang benar.
Selain itu, tak ada yang tahu apa pun tentang dirinya.
Kabarnya ia pertama kali muncul di sini berabad-abad lalu. Burung-burung hitamnya adalah utusannya, yang mampu terbang ke masa lalu maupun masa depan, dan melalui mereka ia memahami rahasia segala sesuatu…

stories.text:
At first, the bird flew through the sky, not knowing where it had been born or where it was headed.
Whenever Blackbird tried to reflect on her past, her memory always came to an abrupt halt at a certain point, as though she had only been born to assume the form of a bird. Yet she could still sense her past that lay before that specific memory: a hidden history, forever burning in her mind.
Her mission had her retrace her steps, all the way back to the beginning.
Blackbird questioned the birds, but they merely chirped back; she questioned people, but they glanced at one another, unable to make sense of her words; she questioned the starry sky, yet the stars remained silent. So she wandered the world aimlessly for four hundred years, flying to the farthest reaches of the horizon and walking every inch of the earth—yet she still failed to find even the slightest clue about her past. In the end, she decided to stop the journey that had long since exhausted her.
"I'm tired. I want to rest," Blackbird thought.
So she accepted Yggash Court's invitation and entered into a contract: Blackbird would use her divination abilities to decipher an ancient, profound prophecy for Yggash Court, and in return, Yggash Court would provide everything she needed.
And so Blackbird moved into what is now known as The Witch's House. After wandering for so long, she finally had a place she could call home. Perhaps that old way of life had drained her too deeply, since for the next one hundred years, she shut herself away in a small, enclosed space and seldom stepped outside again.
Just when she thought her days would go on like that forever, something shattered the status quo. On an otherwise ordinary day, she reached for an Oracle Stone to purify it, as per usual. The moment her fingers touched it, however, a pain unlike any other overwhelmed her. Yet Blackbird did not give up. Even when the pain made her faint countless times, she kept trying again and again, striving to purify the soul attached to it—not only out of compassion, but also out of a stubborn need to prove her own existence. By the time the pain almost reached its zenith, Yggash Court sent many doctors to examine her, yet none could determine the cause of her illness. From then on, she was left with a lingering condition that she would have to endure forevermore.
Even now, whenever Blackbird touches an Oracle Stone, she still feels that searing pain. But unlike before, she has fully accepted it, and perceives it as some revelation. Yggash Court no longer needs to worry over it, either—Lavinia, the specialist ostensibly assigned to help with Blackbird's daily needs, is watching over her and reporting her movements back to them. Blackbird has never voiced any objection to this. Until the work is finished, Yggash Court naturally does not want her falling ill again or leaving, and Blackbird understands completely.
Now, Blackbird's life has settled back into peace. With the help of Yggash Court and Lavinia, she has come into contact with many new things she had never seen or heard of before. She tried starting an online divination business, and her work only grew busier from there. It was around that time that the title "Witch" began to spread on Bagel. More and more customers came to her for divinations, and she was happy to use her crystal ball to help people sort out their worries. Seeing her customers smile and hearing their thanks, Blackbird felt a deep sense of fulfillment from the bottom of her heart.
Later, a bird came to rest on a branch. The shadows over its fate were scattered by starlight, and it rested there in a calm stillness, waiting for its next journey.

stories.title: Savior
stories.text:
When the first tongue of flame leapt up from beneath her feet, even Merula's lips would not stop trembling.
Her naive heroism vanished without a trace in the face of the fate closing in on her. Merula fought back the urge to run, but when the sweltering pain rose through her calves, she truly understood how terrifying death could be.
It hurts… it hurts…
Her whole body erupted in a raging inferno. Merula wept and screamed. The pain was countless times worse than she had imagined, and all she could do was beg helplessly for help. Her faint voice was drowned out by the song of the surrounding crowd, that mournful singing growing louder and louder, like a tempest.
The figures in the crowd, including the Inquisitor, wavered in the shimmering heat. In her haze, Merula saw the Devil leering at her.
…I want to become… a real… Witch…
Merula pleaded in despair. If there was no escaping this fate no matter what, then if she became a Witch, could this absurd slaughter finally cease?
At least… I could save everyone…
Merula dimly remembered the Devil agreeing to her bargain, the price being half her soul in exchange. In the next instant, a spark tore free from her chest, now blackened like charcoal. The spark circled in the air, then soared further and further away. Merula forgot everything. Though the surging flames blocked her sight, she remained steadfast, staring blankly in the direction that singular spark had gone.
Live on…
Once its presence disappeared into the flock of birds and could no longer be found, boundless fear and loneliness replaced her resolve and swallowed her whole. She felt pain again. She did not want to die. She did not want to suffer. She wished to call out for that spark, to beg it to take her away. A tear fell from her empty eyes, then more followed, dripping to the ground and gathering into a river of sorrow.
The Inquisitor's laughter stopped. The burning agony subsided. A strange silence fell over everyone. Merula stood dazed at the stake and saw the frightened looks on everyone's faces, and the Inquisitor's face twisted with rage.
"Merula… Merula is a Witch…!"
It was as if she was a million miles away, the voices barely noticeable. However, it was that distant, far-off line that she would hear again and again for the next several hundred years. A pain unlike fire swept through her body and soul. With great effort, she raised her head and saw a gigantic "cage," vast as the sky, gradually taking shape. Centered on Merula, it fed on her blood and flesh and spread outward without end, as if it meant to shroud the entire world.
"The witch hunt" was then brought to a halt, just like that.
The furious Inquisitor roared, threatening Merula and ordering her to withdraw this bizarre "cage," but Merula could hear nothing anymore. Her body gradually grew smaller, from a girl into a child, and from a child into an infant. At last, she vanished, leaving not even a drop of blood behind.
Driven by the maddened Inquisitor, the deadly blaze burned within the cage for many days and nights. By the time Merula was finally able to completely control her new body, she brought down a rain of blood to extinguish the flames. The town from her memory had long since turned to ash. Across the ground where everyone had once stood lay countless black Oracle Stones. She heard the wailing of souls. She heard the Inquisitor's shrill laughter. It's all right, though. They can never escape again. Merula could only comfort her heart, overflowing with terror and remorse, using those words. No one would die because of the Devil ever again. The Devil that brought calamity would never be able to do evil again.
We have no reason to blame a girl so kind, yet so foolish. Poor Merula desperately tried to make up for the disaster she had caused. For hundreds of years, she remained vigilant, guarding against any possible sign of the Devil. She would ensure that people elsewhere would never suffer the same misfortune, that their tears of despair would no longer fall, and for the sake of that pure and naive wish—to become a true savior for all.
But where was her savior?
Outside the cage, the birds flew for one hundred years, then another hundred. All things slept in the night, and then were awakened by dawn. Only the first second of eternity had passed, and the starry sky still remained the same.

stories.title: Journal I: Wings at Rest
stories.text:
"Birds in the sky never know they are the stars of the day."
Long, long ago, I too was once one of those stars.
My earliest memory begins with a spark. I remember the sun being so close that everything around me was perpetually burning. Countless birds like me were fleeing in desperation. I heard someone's voice, but I did not dare to look back. I don't know how long I flew. Only when the last flame on my feathers was snuffed out by the wind did I come to rest by a lake, where I saw a patch of black in the water blinking back at me.
"Blackbird" became my name.
I flew through the sky, yet the birds never saw me as one of their own, never joined me in flight. I walked the earth, yet people saw me as an outsider. They either drove me from their lands or treated me as a divine envoy of portent—because my innate ability to know nearly everything was, to people then and now, both terrifying and irresistible.
But I cannot divine my own fate. I can see the past and future of others, yet I do not know where I was born or where I'm meant to go. So I simply followed the wind. I saw countless living beings, and I saw their fates shining beneath the stars. I envied them. They had homes, memories, and somewhere to return to. Their lives were brief, yet straightforward and complete. Birds or humans—everyone needs a reason to exist. So what about me? What was the meaning of my coming into this world? I spent a hundred years flying in the sky, and another hundred walking the earth, yet no matter how I searched, I never found an answer.
As time goes on, it slowly wears away many things, including the passion to search for my memories. I have grown tired of this fruitless search. I am weary. I want to fold my wings and stop—maybe even find some place to lie down and sleep, with birdsong and the swaying leaves around me. Sometimes, I wonder if the real me perhaps died long ago, and what now wanders the world is nothing more than a lone spirit.

stories.title: Roostcall
stories.text:
Long ago, Yggash Court noticed this weary old bird—or, more precisely, her unusual foresight. So, when Blackbird was unsure where to rest, Yggash Court extended an olive branch: if she was willing to help them with one task, they would provide her with a safe place to stay, ample food and water, and anything else she needed.
Almost without a second thought, she accepted their suspiciously generous offer. Blackbird had never heard of this so-called Yggash Court before, yet she didn't care. All they wanted was for her to unravel a prophecy's hidden meaning, and solving riddles was what she did best. Yggash Court hadn't lied to her, either. After signing the contract, they led Blackbird to her new home. The moment she stepped inside, Blackbird knew she would spend the next one hundred years there. As if by design, every decoration had been arranged to her liking. Even the chairs were of perfect height. Standing in the room, Blackbird felt, for the first time in her life, like she had finally returned home.
Perhaps she had wandered for too long, or perhaps she had grown too attached to the idea of a "home," but after that Blackbird rarely left. She read, wrote, stargazed, and organized her collections. Blackbird liked anything that took a very long time to finish. Time wasn't worth cherishing. That might sound harsh to others, but to Blackbird, life was the only thing she could afford to spend so freely.
Perhaps she had been too confident in her own abilities; when Blackbird realized she couldn't finish the work assigned to her so easily, she felt an unprecedented sadness. But only a few days later, she pulled herself together again—she had thought of the possible link between this prophecy and her own fate, and the idea nearly made her tremble. If she could uncover her missing memories, if she could see her destiny clearly… even if the odds were only one in a million, it was a sign of something she had never experienced before. Blackbird then decided to see this humble job through to the end.
As for how long it would take to unravel that obscure prophecy, Blackbird was unsure. Yggash Court's terms never specified a deadline. Maybe a hundred years, or two hundred—perhaps even longer. Blackbird always reminded herself, though: "No matter how long it takes, I will finish it."

stories.title: Journal II: Under Her Wing
stories.text:
"I'm Lavinia. Dispatched by Yggash Court, I'll be your guardian from today on."
I can still remember the morning Lavinia first arrived. I had just pulled an all-nighter and was forced out of bed, so I listened in silence, exhausted, as she read off those long, tedious terms: "I'll come by at eight every morning, and during working hours I'll stay in the office until seven in the evening. Miss Blackbird—if I may call you that—please don't mind me. If you need anything, just let me know." With that, she gave me a stiff bow, as dull and severe as she was. "How did they describe me to you, Lavinia?" "Miss Blackbird, I trust only what I see with my own eyes." The woman in front of me bowed again, then started to sweep through The Witch's House like a lioness patrolling her territory. "It's a necessary part of my work," she explained, "but I won't enter your private space without permission." She kept her word. For years after that, she never once set foot in my attic. Even when I blasted movies at a ridiculous volume, she never complained. I have to admit, I was quite happy with that.
It took us several years to get even a little familiar with each other. I didn't have much need for conversation, and she mostly kept herself shut in the office during working hours. She seemed to treat me more like a coworker than someone she was monitoring. The dining room became the place where we talked the most. "Miss Blackbird, please sit in the chair, not on the table." "Miss Blackbird, don't forget to take your medicine after purifying an Oracle Stone." "Miss Blackbird, there's a document I'll need you to look over later." "Lavinia, if your words were as tasty as your cooking, that'd be great." "Miss Blackbird, I put careful thought into everything I say to you, just as I do with everything I make for you."
Every week or two, she'd report my condition to Yggash Court. The Witch's House is a cage, though warm and comfortable… Please don't misunderstand. I have no issue with Lavinia herself or with Yggash Court. They have provided me with everything I could ever need. Until the job was done, they were probably afraid I'd fall ill again like before, or disappear one day without warning. I can understand why they went to such lengths to assign a so-called "guardian" to keep tabs on me. Even going out requires a guardian's permission or escort. But sometimes I think they're a little too cautious. Usually, only supermarket sales can push me to go outside. Still, every so often Lavinia would take me out for a walk—either to the Bureau to file documents, or to handle some other procedure. I wanted to drive, but she never let me.
Lavinia and I lived together peacefully like that for a long time. Compared with when she first arrived, our relationship had come a long way—or at least, I think so. She no longer called me "Miss Blackbird," and now and then she'd even strike up casual conversation on her own. She still kept her distance, but I could feel her slowly beginning to treat me like a "real" person. And honestly, I think I'm starting to enjoy being "real."

stories.title: Sweet Dreams, Merry Wake
stories.text:
Blackbird's other "job" was purifying the Oracle Stones scattered across the world.
This was not a task given to her by Yggash Court. Instead, back when she wandered the world on foot, she had deliberately sought out those unusual stones. From the first time she touched an Oracle Stone, a subtle pain flared at her fingertips, and so she knew they shared some hidden, profound connection to her past. After entering into a contract with Yggash Court and ceasing her wanderings, she told the birds: if you find these glittering stones, no matter how far away, bring them back to me.
Every day, The Witch's House would receive Oracle Stones, some crimson, some black as pitch. Once Blackbird purified them, their murky color would be washed away by a pure light, and the souls churning within them would be set free. Purifying Oracle Stones was as instinctive to Blackbird as searching for her memories. Whenever the souls' cries gradually fell silent, she felt her own heart grow peaceful.
The change came on an ordinary day. As usual, Blackbird went to remove an Oracle Stone from a bird's beak. But the moment she touched it, a violent pain unlike anything before swallowed her consciousness. During that brief blackout, she dimly felt the world turn into a sea of fire. Shrieking tongues of flame licked at her skin. She wanted to become a bird and flee, but someone was crying out, clutching her wrist in a desperate grip and begging her not to go. Blackbird could only watch as the blaze devoured her bit by bit. A mourning song drifted from far away, and fear and pain forced a scream from her throat. When she struggled awake, the agony was beyond anything she had ever felt.
When her mind finally cleared, she saw the Oracle Stone had dropped onto the floor beside her. Without hesitating, she picked it up again.
The pain spread through her body again, like a blaze. Blackbird did not know how many times it made her faint before she finally purified that Oracle Stone completely.
"If those souls are enduring such suffering now… then I must purify them all—as many Oracle Stones as I can, as quickly as possible." Blackbird stroked the stone, now clear and translucent, and silently made up her mind.
And she kept her word. Far from frightening her, the pain only strengthened her resolve. It took Blackbird decades to grow used to it, from fainting again and again from the agony to purifying a whole Oracle Stone without the slightest change in expression. Even as the pain spread day by day to more parts of her body, even as nightmares filled her with dread the moment she closed her eyes, to the Blackbird of that time, that bone-deep pain was no longer tormenting her. It had become the proof she had desperately craved ever since she came into being: that she had purpose.
Blackbird fell into an obsession of compassion. She feared the pain, and yet longed for it with all her heart. The crying in her dreams grew ever more piercing, but Blackbird herself became quieter and quieter. For a long period, she no longer had the strength to manage even her daily life. Yggash Court noticed something was wrong and sent many skilled physicians to examine her, but not one of them could identify the root of the strange illness. In the end, all they could do was prescribe painkillers that treated the symptoms, but not the cause. They attributed it to overwork, and forced her to take leave, ordering her to stop working and rest.
During her recovery, Blackbird spent night after night on the rooftop, gazing up at the vast, boundless starry sky. The cold stars still hung there in silence, but this time, in that silence, Blackbird seemed to receive many truths. She learned to use medicine to ease her pain, and began to "purify" herself just as she purified Oracle Stones. When her heart returned to stillness, everything seemed to come back under control. In another dream, Blackbird no longer tried in vain to break free from the person holding her. Instead, she turned and searched for them, then gathered that person into her arms amid the endless fire. The crying stopped. The mournful song vanished as well, replaced by everyone's laughter. Just before the sea of flames completely devoured her for the last time, Blackbird lowered her head and saw a smiling face exactly like her own.

stories.title: Journal III: The Witch Off Duty
stories.text:
"The Witch's House is a shell that keeps time sealed inside forever."
Unlike the old things in my collection room, I'm an "old thing" that's quite happy to embrace new things. Yggash Court periodically sends over supplies they think are necessary, and that includes the phone I use now.
I have to admit, it's hard to believe how much the world changed during the century I spent shut away inside. After I learned to use this device, Yggash Court no longer had to keep watch on me all the time, and Lavinia gradually realized her real job was to make sure I actually got back to work. I once set a record by watching horror movies for 58 consecutive hours. If Lavinia hadn't finally lost it and cut the internet, I probably could've gone another 20.
I don't think spending so much time on my phone is a bad thing. With this little box, I can stay in sync with the outside world without even leaving the house. I've also learned a lot of new things, like how to drive a car. By the way, I've set and still hold the fastest completion times in several racing games.
More than that, I've never slacked off because I was having too much fun—quite the opposite, in fact—I've actually gotten busier. I created an account on Bagel and tried running an online business, and to my surprise, it turned out pretty well. Thanks to where I live and my own mysterious nature, "the Witch who lives in The Witch's House" gradually became known to more and more people. Oh, and "Witch" and "The Witch's House" are the names my friends on Bagel came up with for me and my home. They also made up tons of urban legends about me, and honestly, those rumors are more interesting than my actual life story.
The busier my online business got, the more income The Witch's House brought in, and I had more pocket money to grab discounted items on sale days… Don't worry—anything I couldn't finish or use up didn't go to waste. Every so often, I'd box up the leftovers and send them to the orphanage. Even though Lavinia already warned me not to throw things over the wall anymore, I still think it's a pretty efficient method of getting rid of stuff. The only real risk is being mistaken for someone up to no good… But as long as I head out at night and turn into a blackbird in time, almost no one notices me.
In any case, compared to the days when I wandered the wilds, I'm satisfied with the peaceful life I have now. If I could, I'd even like to stay in The Witch's House forever… Still, one day the prophecy will be made clear, and the bird that's only been roosting here for a while will spread its wings and take flight again. No matter what fate has in store for me, I will accept it gladly.

stories.title: Journal IV: The One the Stars Sent
stories.text:
Well then, you could probably take the grand prize in a "How Well Do You Know Miss Blackbird?" contest by now. I've rambled on quite a bit—I hope you haven't gotten tired of it yet.
I'm honestly surprised that anyone would be so deeply interested in my story, and it's left me a little flustered… Truth be told, I hadn't planned to write this much. My past has been long and rather dull, like a tedious, predictable movie with no climax worth waiting for. If I were to record every story from those hundreds of years, it might take about the same amount of time all over again. So I picked out just a small part to write down, and I hope I didn't bore you to death.
In the life I've lived, I've seen countless meetings and farewells. To me, people and birds are much the same—both only rest on a branch for a mere moment before quickly leaping into the boundless sky. I never expected to meet you, but I've already prepared myself for any parting the future may bring… Ah, please don't misunderstand. That's just the usual way a diviner thinks. One day, you'll go where you need to go, and meet all the people you need to meet. Our paths have crossed for only a moment, but being able to open my heart to you like this means more than I can say.
I can't see your past, but I can see that your road ahead will shine bright like the stars. No matter where fate leads us from here, I sincerely wish you happiness.
In any case, since our fates have already been decided, please don't worry too much about what I've said. At least in this moment, as you read these lines, I'll be by your side, sharing these feelings with you.

Langsung mendapat Malice saat memasuki pertarungan. Malice tidak bisa didapat selama dalam status Witch of Deliverance. skills.quote: Untuk api, daging dan tulang; untuk langit, bulu dan cakar.

skills.quote: Ia datang ke negeri ini dan memberkati bumi. Dan orang-orang memuji-Nya, menyanyikan-Nya, menghidupi-Nya, dan memangsa-Nya. "Ah! Betapa tanpa pamrihnya sang juru selamat itu!"

skills.quote: "Seratus tahun untuk mengembara, seratus tahun untuk terbang, seratus tahun untuk mencari, seratus tahun untuk bernyanyi."

"Siapa yang menyelesaikan semua tugas hari ini? Padahal aku baru mau berangkat!"

stories.text:
The core strikeforce of ETD-6, the one who gets things done, the blade that swings at every anomaly crime.
"Can I really say that? Isn't that exaggerating a bit?"
"It's cooler than 'Your friendly ETD-6 member' for sure."

Most people's first impression of Chaos is "that weirdo with the mask." At first, they find Chaos unapproachable, but as long as they spend some time with him, they'd realize that he's joyful, cheerful, and easy-going. The moment you start talking to him, the conversation flows like a tide, until he catches himself talking too much, or the listener becomes impatient, or a new mission notification rings.
In combat, however, he transforms into a battle junkie. His willpower is as strong as iron; he never runs out of stamina, and he refuses to let go of his targets. Sometimes, he's so eager to catch a criminal, that he ignores everything else, such as the Bureau's rules and regulations. If you ask him about the rules, he'll likely admit that he's never figured out the Bureau's red tape or hierarchies. In fact, sometimes, he even forgets he works for the Bureau. Fortunately, he works for one of the most flexible units in the organization.
His teammates in Unit 6 don't mind his quirks. It helps that their all-capable captain can always handle the fallout, so Chaos's habit of ignoring processes has arguably improved the team's performance. The captain, who handles cleanups personally, has made no comment on the matter.

Chaos's Esper ability is summoning a mass of smoke that can be shaped into solid forms. The amount of smoke isn't fixed, but it never drops below a certain level. Chaos believes the output of his smoke corresponds to the past crimes of those around him, as he'd always generated more smoke in places with a criminal history. Still, that's only his theory. The actual mechanism remains unknown.
"Is that how my powers work?"
"Hey, why would you think I know your powers better than you?"

stories.title: Graveyard Keeper
stories.text:
Before working for the Bureau of Anomaly Control, Chaos was once the graveyard keeper for Ghroth Island. He was responsible for overseeing criminals, not knowing that he would be catching criminals in the future.

Eventually, a major incident—the jailbreaking of a dangerous Esper criminal—would push him to join the Bureau. Though it was not his fault, Chaos blamed himself for not monitoring the inmates more effectively. To make up for his mistake, he swore that he'd put in Ghroth Islalnd every criminal who deserves to be there. Only after that, would he return to meet the warden.
Since no one could hold back Chaos once he made up his mind, the warden, who didn't want to overstep and cause trouble to the BAC, entrusted him to the Bureau and transferred him to ETD to deal with anomaly crimes.

stories.title: Boulder
stories.text:
Before entering Ghroth Island, Chaos was an Anomaly Hunter on a small island, where he went by his old name, Conrak. Eventually, he would abandon the name he received from his parents like a sunken boat in the sea.

Conrak once got into a shipwreck with another 11 crewmates. They found themselves in an ocean isolated from the world.
There was an archipelago in the ocean, which didn't even have internet access. Conrak and his crewmates settled on one of the islands but never stopped wanting to go back. Unfortunately, no islander was willing to leave their home to ferry them across unknown waters, and no outside vessels passed through the islands. The group decided to build a ship and sail home by themselves. They named the ship "the Boulder."
Once they built the Boulder, the group began to save up supplies for their return trip. For two years, the group navigated the Boulder around the islands to transport goods for funds. Since the group members were also Anomaly Hunters, they often took commissions, solving many issues that plagued the islanders. Gradually the "Boulder Hunters" became known local heroes.
In the end, because the group lived peacefully on the islands and was praised as heroes, some of them no longer wished to risk another adventure to return. Only five of them decided to go back.

However, on its return journey, the Boulder went through a storm. Conrak fell into the sea, and his companions weren't able to find him.
Luckily, Conrak fell into the sea near Ghroth Island and was saved by an Undertaker from the Island.
Once he formally joined Ghroth Island, Conrak changed his name to Chaos.

stories.title: Starting Point
stories.text:
Long before the Boulder went on its adventures, Conrak was an ordinary boy living in a small seaside town. The sea was calm, and he would often stand at the shore gazing at the water, with no way of seeing the storms that would occupy the second half of his life.

When Conrak was 13, his parents put him on a boat to travel far. They said they were preparing Conrak for the life of a sailor.
Conrak didn't know that his parents didn't love him, nor did he know that he was seen as a burden to their struggling family. He merely believed that he would become a sailor, make a great deal of money, then take his parents somewhere far away for a happier life. He even brought home a dog, feeding it out of his own pocket money, hoping that when he was away, the dog would look after his parents.
Conrak opened the last bag of dog food and kissed the dog on the cheek, then waved at his family and boarded the ship, not knowing it would never return.
In fact, the ship was a smuggler's ship, and its destination was an uninhabited island, though it never got there.
Midway through the voyage, the ship sank in a storm. Conrak awakened his Esper Ability, and black smoke took shape in the form of a ship. He and the other survivors miraculously made it through, carried by their abilities—only to find themselves in an ocean isolated from the rest of the world.
From here unfolds the story of the 17-year-old Conrak and his companions.

stories.title: Fortelling
stories.text:
"You will die with infamy."
Chaos found himself on the receiving end of such foretelling. When they were still building the Boulder, a mysterious old person stopped him suddenly and left him with these words.
Somehow, Chaos never forgot them. At times, he would tell himself that unfounded words aren't worth dwelling on, but whenever a mission goes wrong, the words would come back to haunt him. Every omen from that island has come true. Even in doubt of his own fate, he brought countless wrongdoers to justice.
That doesn't mean he pursues justice to defy the omens. He's had a passion for fighting evil and upholding good since he was young. The fortelling simply stirred a hidden, rebellious streak in him, making him more driven, until he became the relentless force against evil he is today.

stories.title: Bird
stories.text:
There was an Esper who went by the name of Icaria on the Boulder. She was short and had a pair of wings, which saved her when the smuggler's ship sank. She usually enjoys zipping around, often joking that she never grew taller because her feet never touched the ground. Conrak called her "Shorty."
Icaria didn't have any parents. She just had an older brother, who liked to make a big deal about working hard to raise her. The brother, however, never cared about her. That's why Icaria decided to stay on the island, though she was capable of flying home herself.
Icaria died when the crew fought an anomaly known as the Kraken. Her wings were not made from feathers, but from some material that melted in high heat. During the fight, she tried to make the anomaly focus on her, but her wings melted when she flew too high and fell right into the Kraken.

After that, Conrak was frustrated about the limitations of his abilities. He tried to experiment with what kind of shapes his smoke could form. Just before a battle, a bird flew past him. He thought that if he could shape his smoke into a bird, he could take to the sky.
This idea didn't come at a good time: he couldn't apply it to the battle at hand, but it was enough to make him regretful… If only he had thought of it sooner, he could have saved Icaria.
Nonetheless, the idea wouldn't have helped even if he had it earlier. 

Chaos is still trying to create flying birds with his smoke. Even after years of practice, he is still only able to create a few small birds that could fly a few meters, unable to even carry the tiniest speck of dust.

stories.title: Torn Page
stories.text:
"In the 600th year, rain fell for forty days and forty nights. Waters rose upon the face of the earth, swallowing every hill and filling every valley until all was made plain."
…
…
He said his name was "Plain," but that didn't sound like a real name. He's a mysterious guy. It's like he knows everything, but I've never seen him in a fight. He likes to claim that he's omniscient and omnipotent, and although he's never been wrong… I just can't help but find him annoying.
Our boat is built. Plain said we needed to give it a name and proposed to call it "the Boulder." Hello??? Wouldn't a boulder sink in the sea? What an unlucky name! The others, however, seemed to like the name, especially that crazy woman with the vines, who said she'll write a heroic epic from the adventures of the Boulder. Is she serious? Plain even gave her his approval, saying that we'll all become heroes. Where did thIs confidence come from?
…
We're actually getting more and more commissions and we're getting more famous. Everyone thinks we're heroes.
Plain has yet to be wrong. I do respect that. By the way, the boat is operational, and we can now call him "Captain." I don't like to call him "Plain," so that's a win for me. Anyway, if he truly knew about everything, why would he ever be sent on that smuggler's ship in the first place?
…
There've been sightings of a monster that resembles an octopus. Many people got hurt. We need to take it down. The captain hesitated for a long time before deciding to accept the commission. I'm not sure what's on his mind. I just know that it has to be us.
During our strategic meeting, the captain kept telling Shorty to not fly too high. It's not like she can fly that high, right?
…
It's over. We won. Shorty died. I can't believe the crazy woman with vines drank too much and didn't show up. This was such an important fight… Had she been there, Shorty might have survived. But thoughts like this won't help…
…
We have enough supplies to go back, but some don't want to leave. They want to be "heroes" here… I get it. We don't know what kind of dangers lies ahead on our way back… but still, I need to return.
I must return.
…
…
Now I realize, my parents knew it was a smuggler's ship.

stories.text:
Chiz stands, professionally dressed, in the gleaming lobby of a bank.
Chiz walks the corners where the streetlights don't reach, sewage pooling under the cracks in the pavement.
"Chiz, Chiz, where are you going?"

Once Chiz learned to run without stumbling, she had to leave home and help her older siblings find food outside. Shiny bread wrapped in plastic… Chiz only saw that once. Most of the time, all she could find were wild vegetables and mushrooms. When even those were gone, they had no choice but to hunt "Apocha." That's what they called the edible Anomalies. But Apocha were dangerous; it was common to get hurt, and medicine was even harder to find than food. And then there was that saying: "Eat too many Apocha, and you'll become an Esper." Espers, like Anomalies, were outsiders to be driven away; because, just like Anomalies, Espers attack. After dinner, Chiz watched her mother cradle her newborn baby sister; patting her, soothing her, singing to her. Chiz remembered when she was little, so little that the whole world was no bigger than her mother's embrace, her mother would gently pat her, soothe her, and sing to her.
"Chiz, Chiz, grow up quick."

Faster, faster. Chiz pressed her palm against the bleeding wound on her neck, glancing back at the Apocha that was closely tailing her. She ran as hard as she could, away from home. Farther, farther—until she couldn't run anymore. Chiz tripped on a rock and fell hard to the ground. The Apocha had vanished somewhere along the way. She didn't have the strength to stand, so she just lay there, nibbling at the food she'd found. She could only eat a little. She had to bring the rest home. Her family was waiting for her. She had to get home… Chiz couldn't remember how she found her way back. But somehow, she made it home with the food… and a new Ability. Maybe, just like the stories said, she had eaten too many Apocha. On her last night home, she used her new Esper Ability to put on a little fireworks show for her younger siblings. She remembered their eyes shining bright, their soft gasps; fighting over who got to play with their magical big sister.
The next day, her mother brought Chiz to the shore. A boat would take her away from home, carry her to a new world. Even after her mother's silhouette had completely disappeared from sight, Chiz could still hear someone calling out in the salty sea breeze.
"Chiz, Chiz, you must…"

Chiz now lives in the heart of Hethereau. Even at night, the whole New Herland District blazes with lights. Chiz often turns off all her lights indoors and leans against the window, watching the flow of cars outside. Back in her homeland, nights were deathly silent. Light didn't mean streetlamps or the moon; light meant danger. It could be an Anomaly's lure. It could be dangerous Espers and their weapons.
Chiz sits in the darkness of her room, while a glittering world sparkles outside her window. She hugs herself, imitating her mother from memory, softly humming a melody still warm with feeling.
"Chiz, Chiz, you must be happy."

stories.title: Old Wounds and Bandages
stories.text:
"The outside world is dangerous." Chiz learned this when she was very young, back when food at home wouldn't just appear on the table. Sometimes, her older siblings would go out and never come back. And then Chiz reached the same age. It was her turn to go outside.
The number of wounds on her body grew faster than her height. The first wound was on her left arm, left by a branch that caught at her while she tried to flee an Anomaly. The second was on her right foot; she stepped in a trap while bumbling down the wrong path through the woods. The third was on her left thigh, where an Apocha bit her before becoming their family's dinner… Some wounds healed and disappeared. Others became scars. The last wound her homeland gave her was on her neck: a scar that remained deep even after healing. In the end, just like her siblings, Chiz went out and never came back.
Chiz boarded a ship headed who knows where; their routes were never fixed, after all. Chiz was unlucky: She became an Esper. But she was lucky enough to find a ship leaving the very next day. All of her mother's love became a thin stack of money pressed into the kind captain's hands. Leave, leave. Staying here will only bring more pain. Chiz began living on the ship with others from her homeland. Some were Espers like her. Others were ordinary people who could no longer bear the strain of staying. But they never really connected, even in such close proximity. One day, two days, three days… One month, two months… Then she lost count. People got on. People got off. The kind captain brought her to a clean, safe city. Chiz was almost landsick.
Chiz arrived at her new home. Here, there were lovely clothes, a warm bed. Delicious food appeared, almost magically, on the table. She sat quietly in a corner, eavesdropping, and learned this was the Dvořák family's orphanage. Chiz loved Dvořák. She loved the orphanage. She made new friends here, and every day they wore the same clothes and ate the same food.
"Why don't you wash your hands?" a friend asked Chiz one evening after dinner. "You should stay clean. You'll trouble the caretakers."
Chiz hid her sauce-stained hands behind her back in alarm. She finally realized that even wearing the same clothes and eating the same food, they were still different. She was a little mouse that had drifted for so long before being washed ashore here. "Mice are the dirtiest of all!" said the picture books. Of course, her friend was kind. She led Chiz to the bathroom and helped wash the sauce off her hands. Chiz was very grateful.
"You have to wash your hands. If you don't, people won't like you."
Chiz was smart. She remembered this. From then on, she washed her hands spotlessly clean every day. Three rounds of soap. No slacking. Clean between the fingers and under the nails. Wash before bed, wash after waking up, wash before meals, wash after meals, wash before playing with toys, wash after playing with toys… As time went on, just like those old wounds, Chiz's hands became wrapped in bandages. The caretakers cautioned her that she couldn't wash her hands so often. Her friends were worried too, gently blowing on her hands and asking if it hurt. Chiz smiled at all of them. "It doesn't hurt," she promised, saying she'll remember.
Much more time passed. Even after all the wounds on her hands had healed, Chiz still kept the habit of wearing bandages.

stories.title: Fons and Letters Home
stories.text:
In an age when digital payments are everywhere, Chiichan still insists on withdrawing her salary from the bank each month, exchanging it for cash, and dividing it into a thin stack and a thick stack. She picks up the thin stack and counts it carefully. Once, twice, three times. Then she takes a few bills from it and adds them to the thick stack before tucking it all into a sturdy envelope.
"This address…" she says. "We don't have direct delivery there." The post office clerk looks at the destination with some difficulty.
"Th-That's okay."
"There's a good chance it could get lost with that many transfers, you know?"
"…Yes, I know."
Chiichan hands the envelope to the clerk. The envelope is stamped; she receives a mailing receipt in return. Walking home with the receipt, a map slowly unfolds in her mind. Chiichan has looked at many maps. On them, the place where she was born is just a tiny dot. If she left from Hethereau, she would have to take a very, very long boat ride to reach a new city, then transfer to a train and ride for a very, very long time to yet another city… If she chose to fly partway, she would have to take a very, very long bus ride… But even once she's figured out the route home, she has to think about the travel costs, and the savings needed so her family could live happily together without ever having to hunt Apocha again. She calculates how much she can save each month, how long it will take… By the time she's done with all the calculations, she's arrived.
Chiichan stands in front of the mailbox by her door, breathing deeply. Whenever she moves somewhere new, the first thing she does is send her new address back home. Then she waits. Maybe today will bring a letter…
"Knock knock." Chiichan taps lightly on the mailbox. "Knock knock." Two more taps.
This is a secret code between the siblings: it means "I found you." When they couldn't speak, they would answer each other with soft knocks instead.
Chiichan opens the mailbox. Inside is nothing but dust. So it is, every month.
Chiichan closes the mailbox and goes home with another mailing receipt. There are a dozen identical ones in her bedside drawer. So it is, every month.
Chiichan doesn't know when she will receive a letter from home. Maybe tomorrow. Maybe next month. Maybe never.

stories.title: Diaries and Proof
stories.text:
Chiz keeps a diary. She hasn't stopped writing since receiving her first journal. She writes down everything worth remembering, so that when she sees her family again someday, she can tell them everything. Then, she'll finally say the words she's been preparing for so long: "Yes, I've been doing well out here."
But her diary isn't just words: there are rice ball wrapper labels, flower petals that landed on her shoulder, and stickers from coworkers. They're all proof that she's doing well. Chiz feels that only by recording things this way can she truly feel like she's not just stumbling through a pleasant dream.
At first, Chiz's diary entries were very short.
"M: XX, D: XX. Food was good."
"M: XX, D: XX. Clothes were pretty."
"M: XX, D: XX. Flowers smelled nice."
She didn't know what else to write, so she just honestly recorded how she felt. Once, a friend found out and suggested, "If you don't know what to write, why not try drawing?" But Chiz didn't think her drawings were all that good, either. She was still troubled.
One day, Chiz ate a delicious candy. She couldn't bear to throw away even the crinkled wrapper, so she put it in her diary. The candy was delicious, and her problem was solved. She's continued to this day.
"Ahhh, how is it this late already? I have work tomorrow!"
Chiz hurriedly closes her diary. Her entries have been longer and longer, lately. There's more and more worth recording. That tasty milk tea has to be written down. Getting praised by her manager has to be written down. The first sunny day of spring, the first sunny day of summer, the first sunny day of fall, and the first snowfall of winter all have to be properly recorded. Chiz doesn't like rainy days. She only likes sunny days, because on rainy days, food is hard to find.
But Chiz really likes snowy days in Hethereau. Snow is clean and white.

stories.title: Cat and Mouse
stories.text:
After completing basic employee training, Chiz's first task at Pink Paws Bank was to get a customer to sign up for a card.
"It's easy," said Mayu, her mentor, patting her on the shoulder. "Our bank has the best benefits in all of Hethereau. You've got this."
"Sorry, I don't need one."
"No thank you."
"Uh-huh, okay, okay, uh-huh, okay, I understand, okay, okay."
Chiz collected dozens of polite refusals and cold shoulders. The air conditioning blasted in the bank lobby; Chiz felt cold inside, too. She huddled in a corner, wondering about resigning. Maybe she wasn't cut out for this job. She was always bad at so many things. She didn't even know how to write a resignation letter.
Chiz would probably remember the day she met Kolinsna forever, with her beautiful golden hair and dazzling red dress. Chiz felt like she was looking at Fons herself walking among mortals. She remembered how Mayu had described it: "Someone who looks like they'd definitely sign up for a card." Chiz really wanted to stay. She just had to try a little harder. So she gathered her courage and walked up. "H-Hello!" she started, "Welcome to Pink Paws Bank… Would you like to sign up for a card?"
The girl with the golden hair and red dress seemed startled by her. She stared at Chiz for a good while, then spoke. Her voice was lovely… until she proceeded to point out Chiz's every flaw; from the way she talked, to her outfit and appearance, to her posture and the angle she was standing at. Chiz felt stares coming from every direction. Tears were already welling up in her eyes. She really wasn't suited for this job after all…
"I'll sign up for a card."
Would Mayu teach her how to write a resignation letter…?
"Hey, don't you even know how to process a card?"
"S-sorry!" Chiz apologized on reflex, then kept responding yes, over and over. Before her brain could catch up, she was already standing in front of the machine. Somehow, despite her fumbling, she managed to successfully issue a card.
"Th-thank you for coming." She didn't know why things had turned out this way, but the result was delightful. After seeing off the young noblewoman, Mayu finally found her chance to approach. She looked at Chiz, who was especially happy about successfully signing up her first customer, with an indescribable expression. "Chiz, do you know who that was?"
"She was… That lady just now?"
"She's the Dvořák family's young lady."
Chiz's smile slowly faded. Pink Paws Bank belonged to the Dvořáks.
Under Mayu's pitying gaze, Chiz choked out: "M-Mayu, do you know how to write a resignation letter?"

stories.title: Gatherings and Friends
stories.text:
Chiz is terrified of loud noises. She's been afraid of thunder since she was little, but it got so much worse after she became an Esper. This is the price she pays for her powers. The sound of popcorn machines, fireworks going off, even karaoke—any overly-noisy environment makes her heart race. Only her soundproof home soothes her. Because of this, Chiz never attends gatherings.
"Chiz, want to grab dinner together this weekend?"
Mayu was inviting her again. Chiz did want to go. She was so grateful to Mayu, the first person to show her kindness after she joined Pink Paws Bank. And it wasn't just Mayu; there was Haruna, Grace… All her coworkers were wonderful people. Chiz had always wanted to treat them to a meal and properly express her thanks. But someone like her…
"I should probably…"
"How about coming to my place? I'll show you my cooking. Come on, Chiz, come on."
If it was at someone's home, it probably wouldn't be too loud…
Chiz finally accepted. She stayed up all night reading posts on Bagel to learn how to be a polite houseguest. If she never got another chance, she had to make this one count.
"Welcome! You didn't have to bring anything!"
"Chiz's here? Come in, come in!"
"Um… H-Hello, everyone…"
The house was warm. There was the smell of home cooking and the chatter of coworkers. So this is what a gathering was like. How nice. Just as Chiz was secretly feeling happy, Grace handed her a box.
"F-for me?"
"Of course! Open it, quick." Haruna leaned in close to Chiz, urging her to open it.
Chiz untied the ribbon. Inside the box was a pair of noise-canceling earplugs. They were beautiful. And pink.
"Pretty, right? We all picked them out together."
"Other than being cute, they're almost completely useless. The noise-canceling is extremely average."
"But they're perfect for our Chiz, right?"
Yes, the noise-canceling was perfectly average… Just enough for Chiz to hear the sound of fireworks blooming in the sky without being so scared that she had to cover her ears and run away.
